title: Why You Should Stop Listening to Get-Rich-Quick “Gurus”
channel: I Will Teach You To Be Rich
summary: Red flags of get-rich-quick gurus (flashed wealth, minimal-effort promises, demeaning jobs and college, fad-hopping) contrasted with slow invest-and-work wealth building.

assertions.quote: they will take videos of themselves on boats stand next to sports cars
these same people promise huge returns for minimal effort
they've jumped from Fitness to crypto to AI to being a LinkedIn influencer and on and on and on

verdicts.note: Fad-hopping is observable, but the survival rate of these promoters has not been measured.

assertions.quote: get-rich quick schemers criticizing college education

verdicts.note: The college earnings premium and the stability of salaried work are well documented, though college is not right for everyone.

The highest-earning business owners are the best educated: 46% of incorporated self-employed hold a college degree versus 32% of salaried workers, while the unincorporated (who earn ~30% less than employees) are less educated than salaried workers, and entrepreneurs are drawn from the comparatively high-paid, high-educated salaried workers; consistent with college and salaried success improving outcomes, though the paper does not test the sales-tactic part.

assertions.quote: they'll make $60,000 from a launch but they spend $58 $8,500 on Facebook ads
I invested 10 to 20% every year since I was a teenager
Focus Less on finding the perfect instructor and focus more on being coachable yourself

verdicts.note: Motivational framing; the components are not operationalized.
